As reported, after firing tens of thousands in the first few months in office, President Trump and his budget director, Russell Vough,t have recently laid off more than 4,000 federal workers across eight agencies, canceled infrastructure and clean-energy projects in Democratic districts, and moved to redirect billions in "unobligated" Pentagon funds to pay troops -- all without congressional approval. The White House has also floated the idea that furloughed workers might not receive back pay despite a 2019 law guaranteeing it. Here's a look at the : Hundreds of thousands of federal workers are furloughed. Thousands more have been fired outright as part of Trump's government "purge." Specialists overseeing the U.S. nuclear stockpile have been told to go home. Air traffic control shortages are already causing travel chaos, with warnings that Thanksgiving could be a logistical nightmare. And 42 million Americans relying on food assistance (SNAP) could lose it next month if the government remains closed. But beneath the economic pain and political noise lies the real reason Washington can't agree: a power struggle over authority. President Trump wants to permanently expand executive power through a little-used provision of the to propose the cancellation of spending Congress has already approved, reviving a process known as "rescissions." Democrats are asking for $30 billion to extend tax credits under the Affordable Care Act (ACA) that expire at the end of 2025. Without renewal, the loss of these ACA subsidies would disproportionately hurt Americans in red states--where ACA enrollment is highest--starting January 1. Adding the subsidies to the resolution would only account for about .05% of the $5.7 trillion federal budget. We need the two parties to come to a reasonable compromise. History tells us it's possible. In 2013, under President Obama, Rep. Paul Ryan and Sen. Patty Murray cut through months of gridlock to forge the --a deal that ended a 16-day government shutdown and set federal spending levels for the next two years. The final bill passed the House 332-94 and the Senate 64-36, with majorities of both parties voting yes. Economic Outlook Meanwhile, our national debt keeps climbing , an unsustainable and immoral tab we're passing down to future generations. The national debt has blown past , and annual interest payments now top $1.2 trillion , more than we spend on defense. Even with $202 billion in tariff revenue , the government still ran a $1.78 trillion deficit this year. The debt-to-GDP (gross domestic product or total goods and services provided) ratio sits at , and that's in a relatively stable economy; one downturn or political crisis could send it spiraling. We're closing in on a debt level not seen since the aftermath of World War II. In 1946, we rebuilt and rebounded, guided by fiscal policies that, over the next three decades, cemented our place as the world's economic leader. , and the U.S. dollar stood unchallenged as the global reserve currency. But now? We've reversed course. As J.P. Morgan strategist David Kelly puts it, My Hilco Global colleague Max Giuliana has an excellent article on , noting that most advanced economies have matched or surpassed our debt-to-GDP ratios, and economists are sounding the alarm. Learn From Ancient History If you're a lover of history, take note of the Roman Empire. The parallels are flashing red. Rome didn't fall because of invading barbarians alone. The real downfall came from economic decay and political dysfunction long before the Visigoths ever breached the gates. Military overreach, bloated spending, and heavy taxation strangled innovation and industry. Sound familiar? The drivers we face today are clear: An aging population. In 1970, just 10% of Americans were 65 or older. Now, it's . Today, Global militarization. Defense spending worldwide increased , the largest annual increase since 1988 (over 9%) Populism and pessimism. Over half of people polled from 31 countries believe their countries are in decline. (via ) And as the dollar weakens-- --the American dream feels further out of reach. For too many, it's not a dream anymore. It's a debt trap nightmare. As I stated on Fox News this week, young men are especially getting squeezed: 60% of young adult men still live at home, 400K of them had taken their own life the last twenty years, and buying a home used to cost twice your annual salary, now it's 5X. Protests Across the Country You can feel the frustration boiling over. Nearly seven million Americans took to the streets last Saturday for the "No Kings" rallies, a nationwide protest of Trump's authoritarian tactics, from masked ICE raids to federal troops in city streets, making it the largest single-day protest in U.S. history. For perspective, the first No Kings Rallies in June generated over five million protesters. President Trump's reaction was to post an AI-generated video on his account depicting himself as a crowned fighter pilot in a jet labeled "King Trump," as he dumps poop onto crowds of protesters. At this point, the trolling doesn't bother me as much as his unwillingness to even talk or consult with the Democratic leadership while millions go without paychecks. Imagine being a TSA agent still working without pay and just watching this mess out of Washington. But amid the noise, there's a flicker of hope--coming not from Washington, but from our local communities. There's a new generation of leaders who are stepping up locally, many of them military veterans. Take , an immigrant, Army vet, and former law enforcement officer running for sheriff in Delaware County, PA, after losing his 8-year-old cousin to gun violence. Or , an Afghan War veteran and Bronze Star recipient running for sheriff in Bucks County. They're part of a new generation of everyday patriots who've had enough of partisanship. (Full disclosure: my PAC, Kennedy Democrats PA, has endorsed and supported both with a $25K contribution.) They're not waiting for Washington to save America. They're stepping up to do it themselves. And maybe that's where our political renewal begins, not in the capital, but in our local communities and states. We need to cultivate more leaders who believe public service is sacred. We're less than two weeks from local and statewide races and a year from the 2026 midterms. History shows that the American electorate will counteract the disgrace they're seeing out of Washington. This year alone, Democrats overperformed in 45 of 46 key elections by an average of 15 points. History tells us this kind of overperformance--like we saw back in 2017 before the blue wave of 2018** --isn't random. It's a sign of a nation waking up. The Democrats were 24 seats away from taking back the House in the 2018 midterms; they won 40. In 2026, they are three seats away from taking back the House (which is why Trump is pushing redistricting in Texas, Indiana, and other Republican states, which is usually only ever done every decade). So yes, the debt is dangerous. People are rightfully pissed off. The politics are exhausting and unproductive. The dream feels dim. But the story of America has always been of brushing against the abyss and doubling down towards progress. The question is whether Washington will listen before the people make it impossible not to. | [](https://substack.com/redirect/e2aa5080-e89a-456d-8ef1-f5ec0893d118?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6480e94a-fd45-4c3e-a8f4-09d7622b0b46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

| Peter,
Trump has been obsessed with renovating the White House in his second term. He's adorned the West Wing with gaudy gold trimming and paved over Jackie Kennedy's Rose Garden to make a concrete outdoor patio monstrosity.

| | Dorian Gray glanced at the picture, and suddenly an uncontrollable feeling of hatred for Basil Hallward came over him, as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas, whispered into his ear by those grinning lips. The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him.

Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. The Grand Hetman of the Crown, the future King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, Jan Sobieski, who knew Sirko well and met him in Bratslav in 1671.

body:
Hi Peter,

As I talk with our neighbors every day, one thing is glaringly clear: Our energy bills are too damn high.

This message was clear at the town hall I took part in last week. I was honored to share the stage with our Democratic Nominee for Lieutenant Governor, Senator Ghazala Hashmi, Senator Schuyler VanValkenburg, House of Delegates Democratic nominee for District 82, Kimberly Pope Adams, and Hope Elliot, longtime community activist, at a town hall meeting on clean energy in Richmond.

Mark Earley Jr. has accepted tens of thousands in donations from Dominion Energy over his political career, according to his own filings.. And recently, he’s advocated in support of Dominion’s proposed Chesterfield gas plant, aligning himself with an effort that critics warn will cause local communities to suffer increased pollution, impacting the health of our friends and neighbors, and causing more environmental damage.

Earley has shown himself time and again to care about two things: his corporate donors and his extremist policies.

We deserve leaders who fight for us, not for special interests. When I get to the House of Delegates, I will push for accountability, protect our environment, and fight to ensure that Virginians aren’t paying higher rates to support plants that poison our air and increase our power bills.

If you’re tired of paying outrageous utility bills and believe Chesterfield deserves better, then please stand with me. Tell your friends. And help us reach more voters so we can expose these deals and champion real change.

body:
In a race this close and with the stakes this high, we need to have the resources to be able to fight back, and we can only do that with your support.
#
Hey, I know my team and I have been emailing you a lot recently asking for your support. But I wanted to take a second to explain why your support matters in this crucial race.
Not only is my opponent, Jack Ciattarelli, endorsed by Donald Trump – he’s also a faithful advocate for the most disastrous elements of Trump’s agenda, and wants to implement them here in New Jersey. He was one of the _biggest cheerleaders_ for the Republican price hike bill that will throw hundreds of thousands of New Jerseyans off their health care.
And now, Ciattarelli’s being supported by a MAGA super PAC that’s pouring _millions of dollars_ into negative ads that make one false assertion after another about my record and my character.
**[In a race this close and with the stakes this high, we need to have the resources to be able to fight back, and we can only do that with your support. Can you split $10 (or whatever you can) between my campaign and State Democrats Committee so we can stop our opponent and protect New Jersey?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/96865?refcode=em20251022-9611&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=9611%2E614464%2Ea3XjkQ)**

But this race isn’t about what we’re fighting against — it’s about what we’re fighting _for._
**My vision for our state is simple: Make life better for New Jerseyans.** I’ll fight to bring health care, housing, child care, and energy costs down, tackle crime and keep our communities safe, and defend our constitutional freedoms from the right-wing extremists who are taking our nation down a destructive path.

name: Chris Pappas
subject: This could be the most expensive race in NH history
body:
This just became one of the toughest and most expensive races in the 2026 election.
Peter, it’s Chris Pappas. I want you to hear it from me first: **John Sununu just entered the race for U.S. Senate in New Hampshire.**
That’s right. This just became one of the toughest and most expensive races in the 2026 election. **[So before I go any further, I have to ask: Will you split $5 or more between my campaign and Wes Moore today?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=partner_ms_cp_em_wesmoore.uhw0Oi&refcode=em-20251022-1&t=3&akid=794%2E1086043%2EF0LTkb)**
**[Chip in $5 ››](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=partner_ms_cp_em_wesmoore.uhw0Oi&amount=5&refcode=em-20251022-1&t=4&akid=794%2E1086043%2EF0LTkb)**
National Republicans spent months recruiting John Sununu because they know he’s their best shot at flipping this Senate seat.
Sununu first went to Washington nearly a quarter of a century ago—then he cashed in, making millions while New Hampshire paid the price for his record. Now he’s running to do it again, and this time he’ll have megadonors and special interests powering his campaign.
**Reporters are predicting that this race could be one of the most expensive in New Hampshire history.** But I know our grassroots movement is stronger than the corporate interests that have propped Sununu up — and this is the moment to prove it. We need to show them that people power still wins in New Hampshire.
**[Will you split a donation right now between me and Wes Moore to show Sununu and the GOP that this seat belongs to the people — not to corporate special interests?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=partner_ms_cp_em_wesmoore.uhw0Oi&refcode=em-20251022-1&t=5&akid=794%2E1086043%2EF0LTkb)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=partner_ms_cp_em_wesmoore.uhw0Oi&amount=5&refcode=em-20251022-1&t=24&akid=794%2E1086043%2EF0LTkb)**
Thank you for standing with me.
With gratitude,
Chris Pappas

Peter,
When notorious MAGA fraudster and former New York Congressman George Santos was initially convicted it was a hilarious time to be on the internet.
Twitter users quote tweeted news stories on his conviction with captions like, "DIVA DOWN" and the ironic hashtag #FreeGeorgeSantos that mocked him as if he were some sort of imprisoned folk hero.
Gen Z memelords even came up with the irony laden "Free George Santos School Walkout," a fictional school walkout that would occur across the nation to show how outraged the youth was over the conviction of this "political prisoner."
---
| [](https://t7pkg9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001yWh81D02r4UiYSwOHMKeKEL6kHFvA0U9bgq4YqWCx67CnyPE7wQ_TKrbhJ_qAvcsnJI6RmFtfmwX_O6apbcJEkbOc-5jHNNIBQIt6-0pSEbntHWcoMYmdGdum4Wsu7fPTzrG6a9rSSutS_FFZess2ej4Ochhka8NhCls7vhqIU3rbOdA5X97pxlO-QR2_S7wDIz1sH4B2DhQCwCbAm_1g_-DyS5uY2n4&c=XDDcMRX1B2j2abwp6ppH-AMAkqdG0VD6sbZbJu-V0LpZnfC8kxw5JQ==&ch=-1c9wG6pFEDEFui40ovV8dMankprpd_7sK92FJBIX8rVuBDq7IDOUw==)
---

But Lauren Boebert, who herself has been caught up in numerous scandals involving campaign embezzlement and wrongful use of campaign funds, developed an unbreakable bond with Santos, going so far as to use her position in Congress to lobby for Santos' release.
Last week Boebert's efforts paid off. Santos was granted clemency by President Trump. She celebrated with a post taking credit for his release and retweeting the "DIVA DOWN" meme.
---
| [](https://t7pkg9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001yWh81D02r4UiYSwOHMKeKEL6kHFvA0U9bgq4YqWCx67CnyPE7wQ_TKrbhJ_qAvcsnJI6RmFtfmwX_O6apbcJEkbOc-5jHNNIBQIt6-0pSEbntHWcoMYmdGdum4Wsu7fPTzrG6a9rSSutS_FFZess2ej4Ochhka8NhCls7vhqIU3rbOdA5X97pxlO-QR2_S7wDIz1sH4B2DiDe0X9jGQAWuvv8--5vSDk&c=XDDcMRX1B2j2abwp6ppH-AMAkqdG0VD6sbZbJu-V0LpZnfC8kxw5JQ==&ch=-1c9wG6pFEDEFui40ovV8dMankprpd_7sK92FJBIX8rVuBDq7IDOUw==)
---
Having made it abundantly clear that she condones what Santos did to his donors and that she is in fact guilty of it too, even Boebert's most depraved ultra-MAGA donors are rapidly jumping ship. This past quarter she raised an abysmal $110,000 dollars.
She is so radioactive and desperate for money that even after one of her top funders was caught running a vicious Ponzi scheme, Boebert ignored calls by Georgia's GOP Attorney General to return the money she received to the victims and the money is still sitting in her campaign bank account.
When Boebert and her Democratic opponent, Trisha Calvarese, a labor leader and relentless fighter for working Coloradans, went head to head, Trisha had the best performance a Democrat has ever had in this district. Boebert on the other hand underperformed Trump in every county.
Boebert is beyond vulnerable (remember she only won her reelection in 2022 by 546 votes) and if there was ever a time to knock her campaign down and fire her, it is now.
We need a flood of small dollar donations today to keep Boebert on her backfoot. [Please, can you rush a monthly donation of $10, $5, or even just $1, to support Trisha. These donations, no matter how small, will add up and give us the long term budget we need to beat Boebert, flip this district, and take back the House for Democrats.](https://t7pkg9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001yWh81D02r4UiYSwOHMKeKEL6kHFvA0U9bgq4YqWCx67CnyPE7wQ_TKrbhJ_qAvcsSU7alfKXV9MlcluYcZbCakzK7VndsnMdEXn2SUgV-nxySM9kvxVXrX2_7Gqt5uAmLawZy2o6u8pOhn37kHudw19Qcgb1M00GG9QxAHckRXl7TN6d2U2OrocnTbQy2xfYhEnfh2IMqMNgAQOONBlZfREGR9DCJZzec5VmDRaI7DiVcTvQQ2SaYennI8J6-0fV_xkVo1Ry-1U=&c=XDDcMRX1B2j2abwp6ppH-AMAkqdG0VD6sbZbJu-V0LpZnfC8kxw5JQ==&ch=-1c9wG6pFEDEFui40ovV8dMankprpd_7sK92FJBIX8rVuBDq7IDOUw==)

Katie Phang--and I went live for another episode of Breaking Bread, and we got real. Not doomscrolling, not outrage bait--real life. Finding steadiness. Pocket-sized joy. **December 30th, 2022** —the night before our New Year’s Eve revival, vandals attacked our host church, spray painting LGBTQ slogans and anti-Christian rhetoric on the walls. We weren’t intimidated or dissuaded. We were up early, scrubbing the walls, cleaning the damage, and praying over our venue. And from that New Year’s Eve revival comes this amazing testimony. body:
hese strikes are a clear test to see how far Trump can go in intimidating Venezuela and threatening violent US military intervention
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=1910%2E791427%2E2uCXaJ)
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em-oct25-venezuela/?source=em251022-1-subs&akid=1910%2E791427%2E2uCXaJ)
Friend — For months now, Trump’s administration has been carrying out illegal strikes on boats in the Caribbean under the flimsy pretense that these boats were trafficking drugs into America.
According to Axios: “The U.S. military has killed at least 32 people in seven strikes off the coast of Venezuela without telling Congress or the American people who was killed, or on what evidence.”
Let’s be clear: **These strikes are war crimes.**
If someone is attempting to smuggle drugs into the country, they should be arrested, given due process, and made to face the legal consequences. Not assassinated at sea by drone strikes in a despicable act of war-mongering. But we’ll never know if the people on these boats are actually “drug traffickers” or merely unsuspecting fishermen.
And there’s a reason that the Trump administration is getting so bold in their violations of international law. These strikes are a clear test to see how far Trump can go in intimidating Venezuela and threatening violent US military intervention.
We learned through a bombshell report from the New York Times just weeks ago that top Trump aides are pushing a regime change plan in which the US forcibly removes Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro.
Now we are seeing the first steps of such a plan come together before our eyes:
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em-oct25-venezuela/?source=em251022-1-subs&akid=1910%2E791427%2E2uCXaJ)
Friend — Regime change in Venezuela is a disaster waiting to happen, both for the people of Venezuela and for the United States.
We can’t afford to get into any more destructive, costly wars. We should have learned our lesson long ago about using our military might to intervene in other country’s affairs against their will.
That’s why we are asking you today to join Ilhan Omar in sending a simple message to Trump: **No War in Venezuela.**
**[Add your name to Ilhan’s petition today opposing any and all military escalations in Venezuela and calling for accountability for Trump’s illegal airstrikes and provocations. We must remind Trump that a vast majority of Americans oppose needless wars and destabilizing regime change.**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em-oct25-venezuela/?source=em251022-1-subs&akid=1910%2E791427%2E2uCXaJ)
**[ADD YOUR NAME](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em-oct25-venezuela/?source=em251022-1-subs&akid=1910%2E791427%2E2uCXaJ)**
No war in Venezuela. We will not be dragged into more endless bloodshed.
In solidarity,
Team Ilhan

Dan Proft Caught in a Lie: Radio Host Blames Lawyer for Leak He Never Received – Receipts Expose False Claims and Coordinated Smear (https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2025/10/dan-proft-caught-in-a-lie-radio-host-blames-lawyer-for-leak-he-never-received-receipts-expose-false-claims-and-coordinated-smear.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=f9478a65ee-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-666344823)
Dan Proft broadcasting live this morning from his Naples, Florida studio. (Morning Answer/Facebook)
By Illinois Review

Dan Proft, the Chicago political operative and Florida-based radio host long accused of blurring the line between media and campaign operations, went on air Wednesday morning from Naples with what he billed as a bombshell revelation. Instead, what unfolded was a blatant lie – one now exposed by text messages, emails, and time-stamped receipts that contradict nearly every word of his story.

On his Chicago morning show early Wednesday, Proft read aloud portions of a confidential 2022 campaign complaint and accused attorney Scott Kaspar of being the source of the leak. Proft claimed Kaspar had personally emailed him the document back in October 2022 – an act he said constituted a breach of attorney-client privilege deserving referral to the Attorney Registration and Disciplinary Commission (ARDC).

But the receipts tell a very different story.

The October 21, 2022 email in question – sent to a small, internal group – shows no record whatsoever of Dan Proft’s name or address on the “To” or “CC” lines. He wasn’t copied, blind-copied, or even mentioned. In short, the document never went to him.
https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2025/10/dan-proft-caught-in-a-lie-radio-host-blames-lawyer-for-leak-he-never-received-receipts-expose-false-claims-and-coordinated-smear.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=f9478a65ee-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-666344823
(Email screenshot provided by Scott Kaspar)
Two days later, on October 23, 2022, Proft reached out to Kaspar by text for the first time. “Scott. Dan Proft. Can you give me a call?” he wrote. Kaspar’s phone didn’t recognize the number – confirming that Proft wasn’t previously in his contacts.
https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2025/10/dan-proft-caught-in-a-lie-radio-host-blames-lawyer-for-leak-he-never-received-receipts-expose-false-claims-and-coordinated-smear.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=f9478a65ee-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-666344823
https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2025/10/dan-proft-caught-in-a-lie-radio-host-blames-lawyer-for-leak-he-never-received-receipts-expose-false-claims-and-coordinated-smear.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=f9478a65ee-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-666344823
(Text message screenshots provided by Scott Kaspar)
That alone debunks Proft’s on-air claim that he’d received the confidential file directly from Kaspar two days earlier.

Even more damning, Proft wrote that he had “heard rumors” about the campaign issue. If he truly had the email, why refer to “rumors”? Why not say, “Let’s discuss the document you sent me”?

Proft also insisted he had “no involvement with the campaign,” yet here he was contacting an attorney about a confidential campaign matter.

Soon after, Proft texted Tom DeVore, the Republican nominee for attorney general at the time, saying: “Tell that f***ing clown Kaspar to go ahead. Please file it.”
https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2025/10/dan-proft-caught-in-a-lie-radio-host-blames-lawyer-for-leak-he-never-received-receipts-expose-false-claims-and-coordinated-smear.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=f9478a65ee-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-666344823
(Text message screenshot provided by Tom DeVore)
The exchange reveals that Proft was not only aware of the developing internal issue but was actively urging Kaspar to file the very complaint he now pretends was improperly leaked to him.

By reading from the complaint on live radio – and falsely accusing Kaspar of misconduct – Proft crossed an ethical and factual line. The text and email records prove he lied about how he got the document and misled his listeners about his role in pushing for its filing.

For years, conservative activists have accused Proft of using his media platforms to wage personal vendettas and manipulate Republican primaries. This latest deception cements those fears. It’s not journalism – it’s orchestration.

The evidence is clear: Dan Proft wasn’t a victim of an unethical leak. He was the instigator, caught rewriting history to smear a political rival and deflect attention from his own behind-the-scenes maneuvering.

His Wednesday tirade wasn’t a defense of integrity – it was a desperate attempt to rewrite the paper trail.

And while Proft now trashes the very campaign that elevated his profile, he had no issue cashing the checks that came with it. Records show he paid himself handsomely from his People Who Play By The Rules PAC, raking in hundreds of thousands of dollars in “consulting” and “media” fees thanks to billionaire Richard Uihlein.
https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2023/04/uihlein-funded-pac-pays-political-consultants-142000-while-spending-just-3700-to-support-conservative-school-board-candidates-disclosures-reveal.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=f9478a65ee-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-666344823#:~:text=The%20Richard%20Uihlein%2Dfunded%20People,candidates%20over%20the%20last%20several

He made a fortune off the very movement he now discredits. The hypocrisy is staggering – Proft had no problem profiting from the campaign’s donors when it benefited him. Only now, after enriching himself, does he turn his fire on the people and campaign that made him rich.

That brings us to where we are today. The very complaint Proft denies leaking ultimately surfaced on his own network of Brian Timpone-operated websites – the same outlets that later amplified attacks by Jeanne Ives, Proft’s longtime ally and now a top advisor to Ted Dabrowski’s gubernatorial campaign, as reported by the
Chicago Tribune (https://www.chicagotribune.com/2025/10/21/illinois-gop-governor-race-infighting/?lctg=443D14D13572C4AB7490B4ED9B&utm_email=443D14D13572C4AB7490B4ED9B&utm_source=listrak&utm_medium=email&utm_term=https%3a%2f%2fwww.chicagotribune.com%2f2025%2f10%2f21%2fillinois-gop-governor-race-infighting%2f&utm_campaign=trib-chicago_tribune-breaking_news-nl&utm_content=alert&utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=f9478a65ee-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-666344823) .
GOP gubernatorial candidate Ted Dabrowski picks up endorsements from former state Rep. Jeanne Ives, former state Rep. Tom Morrison and former DuPage County Auditor Bob Grogan. (Photo credit Rachel Pierson)
What began as a confidential campaign matter in 2022 was transformed into a public smear – pushed through Proft’s media operation and weaponized by Ives to benefit Dabrowski, who is now running against Darren Bailey for the Republican nomination for governor.

After all the lies, deflections, and finger-pointing, one truth remains unmistakable: Dan Proft didn’t just cover the leak – he and Jeanne Ives were the leak.

# Fall Fashion with a side of Communism
Retail giant **[Target has sparked outrage](https://substack.com/redirect/6d3716d4-a7db-4f9a-a95a-61c56677da33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after slipping Karl Marx's anti-capitalist manifesto "Capital" into Instagram ads for women's fall scarves and boots, targeting urban female shoppers amid the chain's desperate bid to ditch its "woke" image following a crippling 2023 boycott.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6d3716d4-a7db-4f9a-a95a-61c56677da33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Ad Carousel Shock:** Instagram feeds unexpectedly featured Marx's "Capital" paperback amid women's items like gray scarves, faux-leather skirts, and gold-buckled boots, puzzling a non-shopper viewer.
* **Irony of Promotion:** The anti-capitalist text, likening bosses to vampires and urging revolution, is being sold by the retailer via personalized Roundel ads using user demographics.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b515de8e-a728-41fb-90a1-70b5cf44be97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Boycott Backlash Echoes:** Target's 2023 Pride collection caused uproar with its LGBTQ+ gear and "tuck-friendly" swimsuits targeted at children.
* **Ongoing Retail Woes:** Nine stores shuttered in 2023 over theft issues in blue cities; shares plunged 7% this summer after naming insider CEO, heightening culture war risks.

# **Construction begins on Trump 's privately-funded White House Ballroom**
President Donald Trump launched a $250 million **[privately funded](https://substack.com/redirect/6d3716d4-a7db-4f9a-a95a-61c56677da33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** White House ballroom renovation Monday, demolishing East Wing space to host grand events easing centuries-old limitations without a dime from taxpayers.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6d3716d4-a7db-4f9a-a95a-61c56677da33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **YouTube Settlement Fuels Project** : Google's $24.5 million payout from a legal battle with Trump allocates $22 million directly to the ballroom, marking a major tech infusion amid ongoing antitrust scrutiny.
* **Corporate Giants Pledge Millions** : Lockheed Martin has committed over $10 million, Blackstone's CEO Stephen A. Schwarzman**** is also expected to be contributions, and firms like Microsoft, Amazon, and Coinbase are also thought to be on the list of donors.
* **Exclusive Donor Dinner Hosted** : Last week, Trump feted representatives from Alphabet, Booz Allen Hamilton, and others at the White House, blending philanthropy with potential naming rights for "The Donald J. Trump Ballroom."
* **Historical Preservation Assured** : Chief architect James McCrery and builder Clark Construction vow to safeguard the site's legacy, extending the East Room into a 90,000-square-foot venue for future presidents' use.

# Wall Street is starting to wake up to the massive private credit bubble they created
U.S. banks have ballooned **[loans to private credit firms](https://substack.com/redirect/57c1d727-0b57-44a3-99a3-d8d8b25c8330?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to nearly $300 billion--10.4% of their total lending--prompting Moody's on Oct. 22 to warn of surging risks for smaller lenders amid weakening underwriting standards and recent regional bank fraud scandals.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/57c1d727-0b57-44a3-99a3-d8d8b25c8330?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Loans Triple in Decade:** Bank exposure to non-depository financial institutions hit 10.4% of total loans, up from 3.6% a decade ago, driven by aggressive post-2016 expansion outpacing all other lending.
**Private Equity Ties Deepen:** An additional $285 billion in loans to private equity funds as of June 2025, plus $340 billion in "unutilized commitments," amplifying banks' overall vulnerability to this sector.
**Smaller Banks in Crosshairs:** Moody's flags heightened dangers for regional lenders if credit checks loosen, potentially straining the broader financial system amid volatile private credit dynamics.
**Fraud Flags Dismissed Broadly:** Recent woes at Zions Bancorp and others have been deemed isolated by analysts, with top executives downplaying systemic threats in private lending despite investor jitters.

# Cracker Barrel CEO FINALLY breaks cover to discuss her woke rebrand disaster
Cracker Barrel's CEO Julie Masino **[defended the abrupt reversal](https://substack.com/redirect/9cfc7ab9-55ac-4064-9825-95bf486a3a39?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** of a controversial logo overhaul Tuesday, admitting poor communication alienated loyal customers amid a stock plunge and President Donald Trump's scathing Truth Social rebuke of the chain's heritage betrayal.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9cfc7ab9-55ac-4064-9825-95bf486a3a39?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Backlash Ignites Swift Reversal** : Intense customer outrage over ditching the iconic "Uncle Herschel" illustration forced the company to scrap the modern redesign just one week after its mid-August 2025 debut.
* **Billboard Visibility Sparks Change** : Masino explained the update was aimed solely at enhancing highway signage legibility, insisting it was never ideologically driven but part of long-term transformation efforts.
* **Activist Investor Targets Leadership** : Sardar Biglari, holding 2.9% stake, launched a fresh proxy battle last month, blasting executives for eroding shareholder value and betraying the brand's rustic roots.
* **Heritage Elements Persist** : Despite the U-turn, Uncle Herschel endures on menus, road signs, and country store displays, underscoring Cracker Barrel's commitment to its "family" traditions amid ongoing remodels.

# Meta dumps billions into planned data center while firing employees
In a bold move to fuel its AI ambitions, Meta Platforms has teamed up with Blue Owl Capital on a **[$27 billion joint venture](https://substack.com/redirect/56c06f48-6ea0-4651-b8d4-ddd3d49d2bef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to build the massive Hyperion data center in rural Louisiana, announced Monday, providing crucial speed and flexibility amid fierce competition with rivals like OpenAI.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/56c06f48-6ea0-4651-b8d4-ddd3d49d2bef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Joint Venture Structure** : Meta retains 20% stake in the Hyperion project, overseeing construction and management, while Blue Owl owns 80% and injects $7 billion cash infusion.
* **Financial Windfall Details** : The deal delivers Meta a $3 billion one-time payout, easing capital strain from escalating AI investments against Alphabet and OpenAI.
* **Scale and Location** : Spanning 1,700 football fields in Richland Parish, Louisiana, the facility demands double New Orleans' peak electricity requirements, underscoring rural site's power demands.
* **Timeline and Rivals** : Construction is targeting a 2030 completion date and mirrors OpenAI's $500B Stargate facility in Texas and Google's $15B India hub in the global AI arms race.

In a fresh round of cost-slashing, Meta Platforms is **[eliminating about 600 positions](https://substack.com/redirect/3ea14088-3303-4c95-b38b-0a9863905ee9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/3ea14088-3303-4c95-b38b-0a9863905ee9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)within its AI research division, the latest move in the tech giant's ongoing efforts to streamline operations amid fierce competition in artificial intelligence.
* **Targeting Fundamental AI Team** : The cuts specifically hit Meta's Fundamental AI Research (FAIR) unit, focusing on long-term AI innovations rather than immediate product development.
* **Efficiency as Core Driver** : Executives cited the need to boost operational efficiency and eliminate redundancies, building on a company-wide restructuring initiated earlier this year.
* **Prior Layoff Momentum** : This follows Meta's May elimination of 5,000 roles across various business units, signaling continued workforce optimization in a post-pandemic hiring surge reversal.
* **Investment Shift Ahead** : Despite reductions, Meta plans to ramp up AI hiring in product-focused areas, aiming to accelerate deployment of generative AI tools like it's Llama models.

Prior Layoff Momentum : This follows Meta's May elimination of 5,000 roles across various business units, signaling continued workforce optimization in a post-pandemic hiring surge reversal. Investment Shift Ahead : Despite reductions, Meta plans to ramp up AI hiring in product-focused areas, aiming to accelerate deployment of generative AI tools like it's Llama models. * The Capitalist is a reader-supported publication Reject Corporate Left Wing Journalism You're currently a free subscriber to . name: Deb Haaland
subject: re: standing on the shoulders of my ancestors
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO
body:
No state in America has ever elected a Native woman as governor.
# [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/133?t=1&akid=5215%2E400544%2EK_Sz-c)
I’m a proud member of the Pueblo of Laguna. I was a military kid and raised an amazing child as a single mom. I’m an auntie, a sister, and a public servant.
But I’m not supposed to be here.
What I mean by that is our country was built on principles and systems meant to either assimilate or exterminate people like me. Either to make me blend into the background of America, or get rid of me altogether.
_But, against all odds, I am still here._
I’m deeply proud of the opportunities I had to break barriers, first in Congress and most recently as the 54th Secretary of the Interior. But every day under this administration, we are reminded that our fight for true representation, equity, and justice is far from over.
**No state in America has ever elected a Native woman as governor.[Can you make your first $5 contribution to our history-making campaign for New Mexico?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/807?c0=em_ms_dh_20251022_1_notsupposedto.QP6Amw&amount=5&refcode=em20251022-5215&t=2&akid=5215%2E400544%2EK_Sz-c)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/807?c0=em_ms_dh_20251022_1_notsupposedto.QP6Amw&amount=5&refcode=em20251022-5215&t=21&akid=5215%2E400544%2EK_Sz-c)**
When I was growing up, there weren’t many women in elected office, and even fewer Indigenous people. How was I to know my path was even possible?
By running a campaign that was brave, fierce, and rooted in the power of community, I was able to stand on the shoulders of my ancestors and prove to young girls of color that they too belong everywhere decisions are being made.
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/807?c0=em_ms_dh_20251022_1_notsupposedto.QP6Amw&amount=5&refcode=em20251022-5215&t=22&akid=5215%2E400544%2EK_Sz-c)_After I was elected, I had the honor of being photographed by Shane Balkowitsch, who specializes in a historic style of wet plate photography._
This is why I believe representation matters. And why I think every single one of us has a role to play in taking the power of that representation to the next level.
**[Together, we can make history in this election. Please chip in $5 or any amount you can afford today so we can build the strong, well-resourced campaign it will take to win this race.](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/807?c0=em_ms_dh_20251022_1_notsupposedto.QP6Amw&amount=5&refcode=em20251022-5215&t=23&akid=5215%2E400544%2EK_Sz-c)**
Be fierce,
Deb

| | Dorian Gray glanced at the picture, and suddenly an uncontrollable feeling of hatred for Basil Hallward came over him, as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas, whispered into his ear by those grinning lips. The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him.
---

Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. The Grand Hetman of the Crown, the future King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, Jan Sobieski, who knew Sirko well and met him in Bratslav in 1671.

My family comes from humble roots.
At five years old, my dad immigrated to the U.S. from Mexico in 1950 at five years old.
After graduating high school, he joined the military, and after serving two tours in Vietnam, he was able to earn his US citizenship.
He then spent three decades as a police officer — a good-paying union job that launched our family into the middle class.
**My father’s story taught me a valuable lesson my parents never let me forget: With hard work, ANYTHING is possible._I carry that lesson with me every day._**
My parents couldn’t afford to send me to college, so I served coffee, painted fences, and juggled whatever odd jobs I could to afford tuition.
I tell you all this because never did I imagine that years _(and several coffees poured, and fences painted)_ later I would be in Congress, and working to defend one of the most vulnerable House seats!
I’ve seen firsthand the change that can come when you work hard.
But when I look around today, I can also see that for so many families struggling to make ends meet, _**simply working hard isn’t cutting it anymore. **_
Donald Trump, and far-right extremists are prioritizing their own wallets and corporate greed over Americans.
**[I’m working around the clock to fight back against Donald Trump’s authoritarian attacks on the rule of law, defend our communities from this administration’s extreme policies, and make life better for all of us. But, the truth is, making the kind of changes I’m pushing for won’t be easy. Republicans are spending millions to keep Democrats like me out of power, and expand their MAGA Majority. If I’m going to keep this seat blue, and continue fighting for people like you in Congress, I’ll need all the support I can get. court to freeze our assets, imprison me, and shut down Powered by
People—Texas Blue Action stepped up to support us in a big way.

While we were tied up in costly legal fights, this proven Texas nonprofit
worked with our volunteers to ensure our successful voter registration
program could continue running uninterrupted. They hired additional staff
to manage the new workload, and they did this at the same time that they
were running their own statewide relational organizing program that will
help Democrats win elections up and down the ballot.

Now that Powered by People has had our right to free speech and political
action vindicated by an all Abbott-appointed Texas appeals court who ruled
against Paxton, we want to thank Texas Blue Action for doing the right
thing. At a time when too many Democratic organizations see themselves in
zero-sum competition, Texas Blue Action proved that working together can
produce something greater than the sum of our parts.

clean_body: I’m running for the Senate against a politician who, while our streets burned, pushed lawsuits against law enforcement officials | Fellow Conservative, My name is Adam Schwarze, and I’m a former Navy SEAL, Marine Corps veteran, and proud Minnesotan running for U.S. Senate against Tim Walz’s handpicked lieutenant governor—a politician even more radical than her boss. I’m requesting your support in this critical battle to restore common-sense conservative values to Minnesota. I hold a Master’s from Harvard, a Master’s Certificate from Johns Hopkins in Security and Nuclear Deterrence, and an MBA. But my proudest achievement is serving our country to make my parents, especially my mom, proud. I want to serve you in the U.S. Senate, fighting for the values that have made Minnesota and America great for generations. I’m starting this race with absolutely nothing , but because of the enormity of the race's outcome, I figured there is no harm in asking for your help. At the end of the day, my request of you will end in one of two ways: 1.) . 2.) you read this email without contributing, but you at least now know who I am. I’m not a career politician. I’m a regular guy from a working-class family who grew up playing hockey and answered our nation’s call on my 18th birthday in October 2001, just weeks after the 9/11 attacks. I joined the Marine Corps to defend our country, and as a Navy SEAL, I deployed nine times to over 70 countries, risking my life to protect our freedoms and way of life. Unlike Tim Walz, who retired from the National Guard before his unit deployed to Iraq, I never backed down from serving our nation during war. Minnesota is at a crossroads. Under Governor Walz and his lieutenant governor, our state has been dragged left by radical policies that fueled the violent unrest in Minneapolis in 2020, defunded our police , and burdened hardworking families with higher taxes and inflation. While our streets burned, the lieutenant governor pushed lawsuits against law enforcement, undermining the officers keeping us safe. This isn’t the Minnesota I grew up in—or the one any Minnesotan deserves. If you are reading this email right now and you don’t live in Minnesota, then I’m sure you’ll agree with me that every American must be represented by individuals in Congress who want to build a better version of the America we live in today—individuals of integrity. That’s not who my opponent is. We have an incredible opportunity to elect a Republican to the U.S. Senate next year - something voters in this state haven’t done since they re-elected former Senator Norm Coleman in 2002. As a Republican, I know the odds are tough in a state that hasn’t voted red in a presidential election since 1976. But as a former Navy SEAL, I thrive in tough fights. I’ve faced worse odds overseas and am ready to bring that same grit to Washington. Here’s what I stand for: Restoring law and order by supporting our police and cracking down on crime. Cutting taxes and regulations to ease the burden on retirees and small businesses. Securing our borders to protect our communities and sovereignty. Defending our Second Amendment rights and traditional values. Stopping the radical left’s agenda that’s eroding the America we love. You don’t know me, but you know what men like me stand for and our reputation. So, . This race won’t be easy. The Democrats have deep pockets, and the radical left will stop at nothing to keep this seat. I’m running to serve you, to protect our way of life, and to ensure Minnesota remains a place where faith, family, and freedom thrive. I hope you’ll invest in me right now – any amount will help. With gratitude, Adam Schwarze Republican Candidate for U.S. Senate - Minnesota FOLLOW ADAM ON SOCIAL MEDIA** | | Paid for by Schwarze for Senate

I am stunned. My opponent, Congressman Scott Perry, just got even more extreme.

**On a conservative talk radio show, he accused Democrats of “hating the military.” Even worse, he accused Democratic servicemembers of only serving as a “credential” so that they can run for office.**

“They don’t care about the Constitution or the nation’s defense,” he said.

I find his remarks deeply offensive, especially to the brave Americans who have stepped up to serve this country. And frankly, I think he should apologize immediately.

This is just one more example of Scott Perry’s extremism — this time at the expense of the men and women who protect our freedoms at home and abroad.

clean_body: Stop the destruction and demand accountability | | | ---|--- Peter, Right now, $9.7 million worth of contraceptives—including IUDs, implants, pills, and condoms originally intended for women in low-income countries—are slated for destruction on the Trump administration's orders. | "CONTACT YOUR REPS" Across the world, women and girls rely on access to contraception to plan their futures, protect their health, and save their lives. "FIGHT BACK" The Center for Reproductive Rights is fighting to stop the destruction and demand accountability At the Center, we've: Supported a Congressional staff briefing to raise awareness on the issue Joined 75 advocacy groups in a letter to Secretary Rubio opposing the destruction Filed a FOIA request to uncover the State Department's internal communications Endorsed the Saving Lives and Taxpayer Dollars Act (S.2252) that would ensure foreign assistance commodities reach their intended beneficiaries Thank you for raising your voice to defend global reproductive health and freedom. In solidarity, Mariakarla Nodarse Venancio Global Advocacy Adviser "DONATE NOW" | | | | ---|---|--- The Center for Reproductive Rights uses the power of law to advance reproductive rights as fundamental human rights around the world. Hey Peter,
The federal government shutdown has officially reached its third week, making it the second-longest shutdown in U.S. history.
Every day it drags on, the impact hits real families in wages delayed, services paused, protections stripped away. Especially here in St. Louis.
Families are missing paychecks and struggling to put food on the table. Essential services are stalled, from disaster relief programs to public health initiatives. Vulnerable communities, already stretched thin, are being left without the consistent paycheck and support they need.
This isn’t abstract. This is real life for real people in our district .
But here’s the truth: our path forward won’t be built on destruction. It’ll be built brick by brick, led by leaders who show up. That’s why I’m running for Congress.
I’ve spent my life on the ground in St. Louis, responding to floods, securing disaster relief for families displaced by tornadoes, fighting for housing, and pushing for healthcare and utilities as basic rights. I’ve delivered millions in relief and resources because I refuse to allow bureaucracy and billionaires to put our families last.
This is bigger than politics. It’s about making sure no family gets left behind, and that the people’s voice isn’t silenced by shutdowns, billionaires, or broken systems.
Right now, Trump and his billionaire allies are trying to silence voices like ours. Your support is what makes sure we don’t stay silent. Chip in today – before it’s too late – to help me bring real results to Congress >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-25q4?refcode=x_251022_shutdown_act]

Governor Jared Polis is also facing pressure after attorney John Case, representing Tina Peters, called on him and Secretary of State Jena Griswold [to ban computer voting machines entirely](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
Meanwhile, Democrats are pushing to restore $600 million in [canceled federal energy grants](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), critics calling it proof of the state’s green dependency, as Denver’s budget woes deepen after [a major tenant stopped paying $650,000](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in rent. Attorney John Case, who represents former Mesa County Clerk Tina Peters, has sent an open letter to Colorado Gov. Jared Polis and Secretary of State Jena Griswold urging the state to immediately discontinue electronic voting systems and return to in-person, hand-counted paper ballots.
Case’s letter, dated October 21, outlines a series of concerns about the Dominion voting software used in 60 counties. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is set to unveil new dietary guidance **[encouraging consumption of foods high in saturated and trans fats,](https://substack.com/redirect/8166939a-b975-4938-8855-ee91cc00d776?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** arguing these foods have been "unfairly demonized" and could be released as soon as this month.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8166939a-b975-4938-8855-ee91cc00d776?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Proposal clashes with current health recommendations:** The shift breaks from decades-long consensus, as current U.S. dietary guidelines suggest limiting saturated fats to 10 percent of daily calories, while the American Heart Association recommends keeping intake under 6 percent, with Kennedy instead blaming refined carbohydrates and ultraprocessed foods for obesity and inflammation.
* **Kennedy says foods like butter, cheese, milk and red meat have been "unfairly demonized for decades":** "New dietary guidelines that are common sense, that stress the need to eat saturated fats of dairy, of good meat, of fresh meat and vegetables ... when we release those, it will give everybody the rationale for driving it into our schools," Kennedy said.

# Victory For MAHA: Walmart Eliminates Synthetic Dyes and Additives From Store Brands
Walmart will remove artificial sweeteners, preservatives, and synthetic dyes from brands including Great Value, Marketside, Freshness Guaranteed, and Bettergoods, according to a statement from the grocery giant.
**[The reformulation will impact more than 1,000 products](https://substack.com/redirect/037385fc-9004-4ede-8a31-a0280d8a9de1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** across categories like snacks, desserts, salad dressings, and energy drinks, with changes rolling out over the coming months and full implementation expected by January 2027.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/037385fc-9004-4ede-8a31-a0280d8a9de1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
## Walmart Removes Additives as RFK Jr. Pushes Food Reform
* **The move aligns with the "Make America Healthy Again" initiative: **Walmart CEO John Furner stated the changes respond to customer demand for simpler ingredients while maintaining affordability. Given Walmart's $276 billion in grocery sales last year, these reformulations are expected to significantly impact American families' food choices nationwide.
* **Kennedy leads the way:** HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is leading corporate partnerships to eliminate unhealthy food additives -- Kennedy has been collaborating with private companies to phase out synthetic dyes and other additives. Major corporations including PepsiCo, Tyson Foods, and Sam's Club have already committed to the initiative, marking a widespread industry shift toward cleaner ingredient lists.
* **SNAP benefits exclude certain foods:** HHS and the Department of Agriculture are limiting food stamp purchases by cutting out sugary drinks and candy. At least a dozen states have received waivers to implement these SNAP changes. Kennedy argues that taxpayers shouldn't fund foods contributing to obesity and diabetes, noting that about 10% of the $405 million spent daily on SNAP goes toward sugary beverages. He emphasizes that Americans remain free to purchase these items with their own money.

## My Thoughts - SNAP got healthier for Americans
One thing that will go unmentioned as left-wing news media reports on this is the fact that Kennedy emphasized Americans remain free to purchase sugary drinks and candy with their own money. Mark my words--the radical left media will only focus on how he is removing food choices from SNAP!!
If anything, SNAP benefits just got better for Americans' health and for taxpayers. Those receiving SNAP benefits will now be better directed toward choosing healthier foods for their families. Over time, the goal is to reduce obesity and health-related conditions, thereby lowering costs for taxpayers. Win, Win!

# MAHA Biomedical Initiative Unites GOP With Shocking Allies
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/68278fa5-1f0b-480b-ae88-ab33d1cc2f08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The National Institutes of Health announced an $87 million investment in a Standardized Organoid Modeling Center to develop alternative research methods that reduce reliance on animal testing in biomedical research.
## Trump, RFK Jr., and PETA unite against animal testing
* **[PETA Partnership](https://substack.com/redirect/68278fa5-1f0b-480b-ae88-ab33d1cc2f08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[:](https://substack.com/redirect/68278fa5-1f0b-480b-ae88-ab33d1cc2f08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) is working with the Trump administration and Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. to advance this initiative, providing information on failed animal experiments and advocating for human-relevant testing methods.
* **Bipartisan Support** : Polling shows 85% of Americans across party lines oppose using taxpayer dollars for animal experiments, with advocates arguing that 95% of new drugs tested successfully on animals fail in human trials.
* **Administration Action** : Trump's FDA head Dr. Marty Makary and NIH Director Jay Bhattacharya are taking concrete steps to prioritize human-based research models over animal testing, using technologies like AI-driven models and organoid technology.

## My Thoughts - So only Kennedy could stop it?
I feel anyone who questions how horrific this can be for animals, should be forced to watch the videos out there of the cruelty these animals go through when tested.
It blows my mind to learn that 95% of new drugs tested successfully on animals fail in human trials. I can't believe no one before Kennedy saw this to be an ineffective way of testing and put an end to it to figure out a more effective way.
This always leads me to wonder what is in it for the organizations who continued to test knowing that testing on animals was failing in human trials.

# The View' Ambushes RFK Jr's Wife Cheryl Hines Over His Policy Positions
"The View" co-hosts aggressively questioned Cheryl Hines throughout an entire show segment about her husband RFK Jr.'s controversial actions as HHS Secretary.
They challenged her about his stances on vaccines, his claim linking Tylenol during pregnancy to autism, and his endorsement of Trump despite the Kennedy family's Democratic Party legacy.
## Watch the clip:
[](https://substack.com/redirect/292a7b7b-b36e-4f36-8341-dd76ea31acdb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
## Hines came to promote her book--"The View" had other plans
* **[Sunny Hostin confronted Hines](https://substack.com/redirect/43b96577-6b02-41c7-abdd-7b6bf63a90ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** about failing to stop her husband from endorsing Trump in 2024, citing friends who had urged her to intervene. Hines defended the decision, explaining that Kennedy and Trump found common ground on issues like lowering drug costs for Americans.
* **Hines defended Kennedy 's vaccine position**, clarifying that both he and Trump support vaccine access while advocating for improved safety. She cited the National Vaccine Injury Compensation Program's $5.4 billion in payouts since 1988 and argued parents' concerns about vaccine reactions deserve to be heard rather than dismissed.
* **Whoopi Goldberg challenged Kennedy 's credentials**, emphasizing he's "not a doctor" and questioning whether his policies remove medical decisions from doctors and patients. Hines countered that 90% of previous HHS secretaries were not doctors.

## My Thoughts - Kudos to Hines
When Barbara Walters used to run The View, I used to enjoy watching it. Although she was a Democrat, she was known for her ability to remain neutral and press for answers from figures across the political spectrum. She always had a conservative host that was allowed to talk without being interrupted or shut down disrespectfully. Once Barbara left, I stopped watching because you could see very quickly where that show was heading--to wokeness!
Kudos to Cheryl for standing firm and responding with respectful, fact-based answers that proved them wrong, even as "The View" co-hosts came at her disrespectfully, trying to make her back down.

SNAP benefits exclude certain foods: HHS and the Department of Agriculture are limiting food stamp purchases by cutting out sugary drinks and candy. Kennedy argues that taxpayers shouldn't fund foods contributing to obesity and diabetes, noting that about 10% of the $405 million spent daily on SNAP goes toward sugary beverages. He emphasizes that Americans remain free to purchase these items with their own money. My Thoughts - SNAP got healthier for Americans One thing that will go unmentioned as left-wing news media reports on this is the fact that Kennedy emphasized Americans remain free to purchase sugary drinks and candy with their own money. See, Scott Perry thinks Democrats hate the Military. He even thinks the only reason a Democrat would join the Military in the first place would be to check a box so they can run for office. Okay, Scott... let's play that game.
#
There's this guy Scott Perry representing Pennsylvania's Fourth Congressional District. He's an Army Veteran. We respect and honor that service.
But, respectfully: Go f**k yourself, Scott.
See, Scott Perry thinks Democrats hate the Military. He even thinks the only reason a Democrat would join the Military in the first place would be to check a box so they can run for office.
First off, and most obviously, 99.99% of Veterans who lean democrat never run for office. The idea that Democratic voters join the military to run for office is asinine. They love their country. Period.
But want to make it about elected officials? Okay, Scott... let's play that game.
How about Dan Inouye? Legendary Democratic Senator from Hawaii, awarded the Medal of Honor, lost an arm fighting Nazis.
Or John Glenn, maybe you've heard of him? Marine aviator, Democratic Senator... First American to orbit the earth in space. Ringing any bells?
Oh, okay, maybe more recent. There's this guy, Mark Kelly. 39 combat missions as a Navy aviator, 4 missions to space as an astronaut. Does Scott think Mark joined the Navy 40 years ago to run for Senate someday?
Or fellow Army Veteran, Tammy Duckworth. I guess Scott thinks she got shot down over Iraq and lost her legs because someday she might want to run for office.
There are literally millions of Veterans, patriotic Americans, who are registered Democrats. Scott Perry represents thousands of them in Congress. And while he talks about how Democrats hate America, our Military, our Constitution, remember this:
**Scott Perry did everything he possibly could to steal the election in 2020 and hand it to Donald Trump. He wanted to throw out thousands of votes from Pennsylvania, including people he represented.**
If that's not hatred for our Democracy, and for the people who fought and died to protect it... Well, we don't know what to tell you.
We're proud to be American, and we’re proud of our service. Damn proud. There's nothing Scott Perry can do to take that pride away. But there is something you can do to help us make sure people like Scott get kicked out of Congress for good.
