| | | | | | Hey team,

We’re on week 4 of the government shutdown.

Our servicemembers have stopped being paid, folks across the country are losing access to services they rely on, and hundreds of thousands of government employees are furloughed or working without pay – including air traffic controllers and teachers on military bases.

And through all of this, has Derrick Van Orden been helping his constituents, connecting them to resources, or advocating for us?

_No._

In fact, Rep. Mark Pocan, who represents nearby WI-02, has been doing townhalls in our district. He’s been answering questions from folks about the shutdown, ICE, and upcoming legislation that could affect farmers and the dairy industry.

I also have been available in our district: I did a volunteer barista shift a couple weekends ago, and for over two hours I was publicly available to answer questions about the City or my Congressional stances.

One thing is clear: Derrick Van Orden is not doing enough in this time of need. He’s not even doing the bare minimum of his job.

We deserve accessibility and accountability from the people elected to represent us.

[**Would you add your name to tell Derrick Van Orden to do his job, fund healthcare, open the government, and be accessible and accountable to our community?**](https://bergeforcongress.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=85565153e5fb51ffb3f8fe008&id=4567e1bfd3&e=a09c3c1942)

subject: Shared challenges. Shared dreams.

body:
#
Peter —
I’m tired of being divided into teams. Because the truth is we’re all on the same team.
* Do you have an elderly grandparent who needs care? So do I.
* Do you struggle to afford the high price of everything? So do I.
* Do you know what it means to carry the weight of student debt, credit card debt, and medical debt? So do I.

You’re on my team, and I’m on yours.
Despite our differences, we all want the same things: a safe neighborhood, a good job, a high-quality well-funded public school, and the ability to see a doctor when we need one.
In an era of division, the most radical thing we can do is bring people together. Not just because we share the same challenges, but because we share the same dreams.
Imagine what we could change in this country if we did it together. As one team, we are unstoppable. That is the promise of this movement.
But it does require each of us to play a role. So I am asking:
[**Will you make a contribution to support our campaign for the U.S. Senate? Together, we can bend Texas and this country toward its promise.**](https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-launch.bF5RK3&refcode=em251022-1-ak&t=1&akid=188%2E1347274%2EGz1xQ4)

You’re on my team, and I’m on yours. Despite our differences, we all want the same things: a safe neighborhood, a good job, a high-quality well-funded public school, and the ability to see a doctor when we need one. In an era of division, the most radical thing we can do is bring people together. Not just because we share the same challenges, but because we share the same dreams. Imagine what we could change in this country if we did it together. As one team, we are unstoppable. That is the promise of this movement. But it does require each of us to play a role. So I am asking: James Paid for by Talarico for Texas Talarico for Texas PO Box 14508 Austin, TX 78761

She has consistently voted for anti-abortion legislation, cheered on the _Dobbs_ decision that overturned _Roe v. Wade_ , and paved the way for Iowa's near-total abortion ban. All of this to score political points with anti-abortion elites in Washington.

Remember, Peter, abortion bans don't stop abortion. They only make it harder, more expensive, and more dangerous for people to get the care they need. And we're seeing this play out in Iowa.

Since the ban took effect, women in Iowa have been forced to travel across state lines to access abortion care. **Clinics in Minnesota and Nebraska report a 182 percent increase in patients coming from Iowa. In our state, only two Planned Parenthoods remain open — down from the many that have been forced to close their doors.**

Each closure represents another woman who has to drive hundreds of miles for care, another working family struggling to find childcare, another person spending money they don't have on lodging, transportation, and time away from work or school. For too many, it means being forced to continue a pregnancy against their will — or facing life-threatening complications without the medical care they deserve when they need it most.

_This is the cruel reality Mariannette Miller-Meeks created, and it's what she'll continue to champion if she wins next November._

It's been 29 days.
#
The government is in full shutdown. Republicans have left D.C. and are refusing to negotiate to call the House back into session.
And now, 29 days after winning her special election with 70% of the vote, Speaker Johnson still won’t swear Adelita Grijalva into the House of Representatives.
You want to know why?
**Representative-elect Grijalva would be the decisive signature on the discharge petition to release the Epstein files**.
But this is not just about Adelita.
This is about the more than 800,000 people in southern Arizona — veterans, seniors, teachers, students — who do not have anyone to call in an emergency because their duly elected representative is being denied her seat by Speaker Johnson and the House GOP.
**But Adelita isn’t backing down**. Yesterday — alongside Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes — Adelita filed a lawsuit against the House and Speaker Johnson’s unlawful interference in delaying her constitutional right to take office.
We need to support her in this critical moment.

Across the country, American soybean farmers are feeling the squeeze thanks to Donald Trump's tariffs and needless trade wars, Peter.

They've lost markets, faced higher costs, and are running out of places to sell the crops they've worked so hard to grow.

Now, instead of standing up for them, **Trump is preparing to send $40 billion to Argentina to support their farmers, not ours.** Meanwhile, American farmers are struggling as China turns to Argentina and other South American countries to buy soybeans. _The president is leaving our farmers to deal with the fallout on their own._

Peter, our farmers feed our families and help keep our small towns and economy alive. When they struggle, we all feel it—from grocery prices to local jobs. Our farmers deserve a leader who will fight for them and understands that farming is more than a business. _It's the backbone of our economy and our way of life._ _We need policies that help local farmers, not bail out foreign ones at the expense of working Americans._

subject: This is why I keep asking.
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Mark Kelly for Senate
body:
You can make the difference.
#

Hey friend, it’s Mark Kelly. My friend Roy Cooper is running for Senate in North Carolina and needs our help. I hope you’ll read the message below from him, and [**rush a split donation between Roy's campaign and mine.**](https://act.markkelly.com/go/1389?c0=mek-em-cooper.oMEak6&refcode=em251022-1-90&t=1&akid=6223%2E6688874%2EhtRAgd)
---
I don’t mess around with something as important as representing my home.
Every race I’ve ever run, I’ve been in it to win — even when the odds seemed long. You’ve been there with me every time, and together, we’ve succeeded. Now, this election for the U.S. Senate may be our toughest challenge yet. So [**when I ask you to split a donation between our campaign and Mark Kelly, it’s because your contribution**](https://act.markkelly.com/go/1389?c0=mek-em-cooper.oMEak6&refcode=em251022-1-90&t=2&akid=6223%2E6688874%2EhtRAgd) could make the difference between victory and defeat.
**Republicans see me as the top threat to their Senate majority. They know that we have the team, the support, and the momentum to win.** That means national attention will be on us.
I will always be straightforward about this campaign: our plans, where we stand in the polls, what we expect to come, and what we need from you.
Right now, we’re preparing for national GOP money groups to spend _hundreds of millions_ against us, and Democrats are being outraised by Republicans. Meanwhile, various polls have shown either a dead heat or us with a slight lead.
[**I am asking you to contribute $5 or another amount that fits in your budget today because we can’t afford to leave this race up to chance — or up to Republicans’ deep-pocketed donors and their dark-money groups. We can win this race, but ONLY if we stick together. Please, split a contribution between my campaign and Mark Kelly.**](https://act.markkelly.com/go/1389?c0=mek-em-cooper.oMEak6&refcode=em251022-1-90&t=3&akid=6223%2E6688874%2EhtRAgd)

I deeply appreciate all your support,
Roy Cooper

subject: Servicemembers deserve to be paid for their work
body:
| | Peter – Last week, active-duty military members did not receive a paycheck for the first time during the ongoing government shutdown.

I co-sponsored a bill to ensure that servicemen and servicewomen keep earning their salaries in a shutdown – as Congress has done in the past – but House Leadership didn’t even allow a vote before sending Members home.

Frankly, it’s a shameful failure of our duty – the brave men and women in uniform deserve better.

So many military members and their families live paycheck to paycheck, and they can’t afford the uncertainty of not knowing when their next payday will come.

[Those who put their lives on the line to serve our country should never have to worry about going without pay. If you agree, please add your name here to show your support for our troops:](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/117793746/577659416/1280335259?refcode=MGP_EM_PT_180DO_251022_1_1_RSNO&refcode2=2d0ac715-88af-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZDBhYzcxNS04OGFmLWYwMTEtOGU2MS02MDQ1YmRlZDhiYTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=cuQaR9VPok7l0kCLKIqEcbNZJPWhru0GLvrz2UyHxF4=&emci=280ac715-88af-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&emdi=2d0ac715-88af-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&ceid=31138575)

Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football’s 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville’s time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year’s Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP’s SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul “Bear” Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime.

Now, Coach Tuberville is running for Governor so he can continue representing Alabamians and Americans in his homestate of Alabama. The Radical Left thinks they can flip Alabama blue and turn it into the California of the South. Can he count on your support? _

clean_body: I just stepped off the Senate floor where I rang the alarm bell about the dangers of Trump’s authoritarianism. | | | | After over 22 hours, I just stepped off the Senate floor, where I rang the alarm bell about the dangers of Trump's authoritarianism. Americans are standing up because the President is not a king, the law is not a suggestion, and the Constitution is not optional. Yet Donald Trump is acting as if all three are up for debate. He's attacking the free press to silence truth-tellers. He's deploying the military against peaceful protesters. He's defying court orders and weaponizing federal agencies to punish political enemies. Every move is part of a deliberate strategy to normalize authoritarian power — and it's happening right before our eyes. Trump is trying to make America accustomed to the idea that one man can rule unchecked, but that's not who we are. Our founders rejected monarchy for a reason — they built this nation on the belief that power should rest with the people, not a would-be strongman in the Oval Office. And let's be clear: Republicans are helping him every step of the way. While families struggle with rising costs and a broken health care system, Trump and his MAGA cronies are using this moment to enrich billionaires, punish blue states, and dismantle the institutions that keep our democracy standing. With them, it's always the same story: families lose, billionaires win. I won't let that happen without a fight. I'll keep speaking out on the Senate floor, organizing across Oregon and beyond, and doing everything in my power to defend our democracy, but I can't do it alone. name: Jason Crow
subject: It wasn’t an easy decision
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jason Crow for Congress
body:
Jason Crow For Colorado [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP21/1/88523/images/Screenshot%202025-08-21%20at%2010.50.41%E2%80%AFAM.png]
Running for Congress wasn’t an easy decision, team.

I came from working class roots. I lived a life of service to our country — from enlisting in the National Guard to serving active duty in the Army after September 11th in Iraq and Afghanistan. I never imagined running for Congress.

But I have always gone where the fight is — and in 2017, the most important fight was right here in Colorado. Just a few months into his first term as president, Donald Trump tried to rip away health care, and rammed through tax breaks for the wealthy and his big donors. Does any of that sound familiar?

And in the middle of all that, our representative refused to stand up. Coloradans deserved better leadership. So I launched my campaign on April 11, 2017. Together, we flipped a red seat blue for the first time in decades.

They say history repeats itself, and here we are: Donald Trump is president once again.

He acts like a king and believes he’s above the law. He uses his presidency to enrich himself and his ultra-wealthy allies. And he’s doing it all on the backs of working people.

Like I said, I’ve never been one to back down from a tough fight.

What we’re seeing right now is not real leadership. I’m ready to fight harder than ever to deliver leadership that serves and listens, and I will work toward a better future for us all. body:
---
| | **ICYMI:
Scott introduced a bipartisan bill to prevent Congress from getting paid unless it does its job and passes a budget on time.**
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/117796199/577667611/983013814?refcode2=ea86b1f8-8eaf-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&refcode=SP_EM_PT_180DO_251022_1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzkvMS84ODA2MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlYTg2YjFmOC04ZWFmLWYwMTEtOGU2MS02MDQ1YmRlZDhiYTQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=5rY0koOR0TF2QnNF0ne2P8MdaRLhE_msG7XiDE1cA0g=&emci=c1291285-8caf-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&emdi=ea86b1f8-8eaf-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&ceid=5258741)
_From CBS News 8 in San Diego_

body:
Our work to win 2026 starts today |
#
---
Friends, We worked hard in all 83 counties in Michigan to win the governor's seat, especially in deep red areas. Because we listened to people and focused on the basics — lowering costs, a good education, a strong quality of life — we flipped counties red to blue across the state. And we won the governor's race by double digits — twice. I’ll never stop being grateful for our work together and the progress we’ve made since. When pundits said it couldn’t be done, we fought like hell and showed up EVERYWHERE with joy and grit. _And we won._ The fights are tough, but we’ve proven that when you cut through the noise and focus on solving problems, you can bring people together and get things done. **Now, we’re taking that fight nationwide ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. Fight Like Hell PAC is hitting the ground to recruit tough leaders, train campaign staff, and bring Michigan’s battle-tested strategies to campaigns across the country.** Last week, you may have seen me hit the road and head to Wisconsin, New Jersey, and Florida to kick off my work to elect people in 2025 and 2026 who share our values. The good news is we're just getting started. Here in Lansing, we’ve worked across the aisle to support our workers, feed our kids, fix our roads and bridges — even when it meant setting aside differences. **That's the kind of leadership people are hungry for, from candidates running for governor, for Congress, and even for local and municipal office.** Leaders who will focus on the kitchen table issues, and leaders who will listen more than they talk. In 2026, we need leaders who will fight like hell for their people. But it's no secret that Republicans are already spending millions to stack the deck in their favor. | | Dorian Gray glanced at the picture, and suddenly an uncontrollable feeling of hatred for Basil Hallward came over him, as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas, whispered into his ear by those grinning lips. The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him.

Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. The Grand Hetman of the Crown, the future King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, Jan Sobieski, who knew Sirko well and met him in Bratslav in 1671.

As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him. | | | Donald Trump Jr. just urged Americans to take action now! He says, “My father's administration is exploring a powerful economic tool that...” Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. I don't back down from challenges. During my time in the legislature, I helped pass difficult budgets, and when it came down to saving the PFD, I went against party bosses and voted with the PEOPLE of Alaska. After winning five elections during my career in public service, I know how to win, make friends, and my experience uniquely qualifies me to be a strong steward of our state. TRUSTED. During my time in Juneau and at the Department of Corrections, I earned the trust of my constituents, fellow Republicans, co-workers, and even Democrats! It's because of my dedication to our state and helping people that I've also earned the title "Uncorruptible". It takes time to gain trust, and I continue to live and work with respect for everyone I meet, even if we disagree. TOUGH. Listen, you'll never get anything done in Juneau unless you have that true Alaskan grit. Don't mistake my kindness for weakness. I'm a compassionate conservative, but when it's time to suit up and fight for what's right, I'm the woman in the arena. | I'm not in this race to be louder. subject: Tell Congress: End gerrymandering
disclaimer_text: Paid for by United for Democracy
body:
They’re playing partisan games with your vote—and the Supreme Court is on deck to help them. | |
---
Peter, **The Supreme Court just heard arguments in a case about Louisiana’s racially gerrymandered maps.** The case gives the MAGA justices the opportunity to gut what remains of the Voting Rights Act. If they do, and given their track record on voting rights it’s not looking good, Louisiana could lose both of its majority-Black congressional districts. **This case comes in the middle of a massive redistricting fight in states across the country.** Republican legislatures in states like Texas and Missouri are gerrymandering their state maps to eliminate Democratic districts by drawing themselves new seats to maintain power in Congress. Democratic governors in states like California and Maryland are fighting back with their own redrawn maps. If the MAGA justices side with Louisiana Republicans, they won’t just be finishing off the last of the Voting Rights Act. **They’ll once again be diluting the political power of, and Congressional representation for, Black and Hispanic voters — handing Republicans the chance to draw themselves 19 new House seats.** [**It’s time to end the partisan games politicians are playing with our voting rights. Tell Congress to pass the**** _Redistricting Reform Act_****introduced by Rep. John Larson and Sen. Alex Padilla and end gerrymandering now.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38jvf5GaclcQ7i_R9B-DMhJxpTJE3HIHzGke8tGHrJP6XXa640Zb7hMYvW6bxzrSWNfXYnKBR4cVCJA9k2qV7453KeO3DlJ9yCaZJZ20xf81IN24oTqUiafXyBP2EdMJNizhVpRX34q7YTaHSWnarF9L3W9sY97bvgVVc-YYOdgNALDKhyMBm_EVqSBLiOKe9JhduneNh1vVCnnJqC7XgrqpJFiYBYfLA8jL8HHb3uKJB8AZ2_WcSWvxbM_nEfSx4tFIolzflhF2Ymem8WbYco9j6z1fJvm24dJi-2LbDq6h_6v3yyT5UgVKzGKH_qQgoQ56MwNENK9WtIPYmjtCSP_WitVWc4q3ztJq0O6LGuZ_iuUkIJ2ztaTrVNQUplRpjc/4ky/BdE2kcmuTSaF341JDDOv9Q/h0/h001._schJlQ5Des0jBeWGuYVNiJ5D7W56RG_de7wxmC5KFs) [SIGN & SEND](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38jvf5GaclcQ7i_R9B-DMhJxpTJE3HIHzGke8tGHrJP6XXa640Zb7hMYvW6bxzrSWNfXYnKBR4cVCJA9k2qV7453KeO3DlJ9yCaZJZ20xf81IN24oTqUiafXyBP2EdMJNizhVpRX34q7YTaHSWnarF9L3W9sY97bvgVVc-YYOdgNALDKhyMBm_EVqSBLiOKe9IT_bleenLyDwIA8nKCHUrbK_r7MLx3gYpo36FIacTkE9jvPdpxxF-kXSSLm19BHl_V-PZnUVeY7TOZ_ukeCHCeBHyKMtlMuFs0d46lb_zBhqdCD151xL1cq33-TPgsAbWEKT_Lnmh6gdQoDy_szqMs98I9Tlss228PBRc_vZc50tiwyytNI_q_He7uI0-h3as/4ky/BdE2kcmuTSaF341JDDOv9Q/h1/h001.roadE5f7RIBBLtoDvKE41zfDK3MDGmfxH-23-ejmcNc) **The Supreme Court is supposed to protect the rights of Americans. But the MAGA justices have shown us they can’t be trusted to side with the people.** Experts are anticipating that the MAGA justices on the Supreme Court will seize the opportunity to further gut voting rights and allow Republicans to racially gerrymander maps across the country. If that happens, 30% of the Congressional Black Caucus and 11% of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus could be drawn out of their seats, according to a report from Fair Fight Action and Black Voters Matter Fund. **In a democracy, we should protect minority votes—not strip them away and create a one-party system representing the wealthy, white, and powerful.** If the Supreme Court won’t stand up for our rights, Congress must instead. # Hakeem Jeffries rejects legislation that would ensure US military gets paid during Democrat shutdown
The White House criticized House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries on Tuesday for opposing legislation that would pay federal workers during the shutdown, accusing him and other **[Democrats of prioritizing healthcare benefits for undocumented immigrants over American troops](https://substack.com/redirect/17030b01-4ba6-45ea-b73a-70f2306fbb0b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.

---|---|---
* **Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., authored the Shutdown Fairness Act** to fund paychecks for federal employees working without pay during the shutdown, with Senate Majority Leader John Thune preparing the measure for a floor vote.
* **Jeffries rejected the bill, arguing it unfairly excluded furloughed workers** and granted Trump selective authority to decide which government employees receive compensation rather than guaranteeing payment for all personnel.
* **Trump issued a presidential memorandum instructing the Department of War to tap fiscal year 2026 funds** to maintain military salaries and benefits throughout the budget impasse, sidestepping congressional spending authority.
* **Democratic lawmakers protested Trump 's executive action as constitutional** overreach, though the president invoked his commander-in-chief authority under Article II to justify ensuring continued compensation for active-duty service members and activated reservists.

* * *
I'll be honest with you, folks--I knew this one was going to hit deep the moment [Dana DuBois](https://open.substack.com/users/201342263-dana-dubois?utm_source=mentions) joined the show. She's sharp, fearless, and funny as hell. You probably know her from _**The Daily Whatever Show**_ on Substack, which she co-hosts with [Lawrence Winnerman](https://open.substack.com/users/314034871-lawrence-winnerman?utm_source=mentions) at [GenXy](https://open.substack.com/users/314515088-genxy?utm_source=mentions).
But Dana's also a gifted writer, chronicling our generation's messy mix of rebellion, exhaustion, and hard-won wisdom. So, when she joined [David Shuster](https://open.substack.com/users/16891317-david-shuster?utm_source=mentions) and me on _Amped Up_ today, I knew sparks were going to fly--and they did.
David kicked things off like the pro he is, asking Dana about her recent piece on the male gaze--about what it's like to watch your teenage daughter walk through the world and realize that too many men still treat women like props in their own bad movie.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/83eb30d1-8632-46b1-9799-0027c66b5d9e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

* * *
David shared a story from his own life--how his wife called out a creep who was ogling their twelve-year-old at a water park--and Dana met that moment with the honesty that defines her work. She didn't sensationalize it. She didn't sugarcoat it. She just laid it out: this is the constant, exhausting background noise of being female in America.
From there, we dug in. I ranted a little--shocking, I know--about how civilization is supposed to mean something. Biology may tell us who we're attracted to, but it doesn't excuse treating another human being like an object. Dana agreed: men know what they're doing. And when they leer, it's not about attraction--it's about power. It's about making women feel small.
What blew me away was how Dana threaded that personal story into the larger collapse of decency we're living through--the way a culture led by a man adjudicated a rapist somehow trains people to look away from cruelty.

* * *
We talked about the AI propaganda video Trump's team dropped on _No Kings Day_ , portraying him as some crowned Top-Gun superhero defecating on his enemies. Dana called it what it was: fascist filth, broadcast proudly from the White House.
David, as always, broke it down journalistically--reminding us that the same corporate media that once freaked out over Obama's "tan suit" can't seem to find the words "illegal demolition" when Trump bulldozes part of the West Wing without oversight.

**🚨North Carolina just passed a new, extreme, gerrymandered map. We’re fighting back. 🚨**
Peter,
Just hours ago, North Carolina’s legislature forced through an extremely gerrymandered map — making it the latest state to rush through a mid-decade redraw, a pure power grab for politicians in D.C.
It was not so long ago that North Carolina’s congressional seats fell along a 50-50 partisan split. But lawmakers passed a gerrymander in 2023, and changed the delegation to a 10-4 split favoring Republicans.
This new map would widen the partisan divide of its representation in Congress even further, in a highly competitive 50-50 state. It also dismantles a district where voters of color have historically had an opportunity to express their political desires.
Our work has never been more vital. All On The Line is organizing to push back against these power grabs. We’re fighting to send a message to states like North Carolina — and any other state considering a similar power grab — that voters will hold them accountable.

subject: Fuel our resistance!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20251022-5552-footer&t=1001&akid=5552%2E420207%2E3-KYDH ]Pramila Jayapal

Peter,

This weekend was an incredible moment for the resistance. On Saturday,
millions turned out for No Kings protests all over the country.

Together, we made it clear that we will not remain silent while Donald
Trump intensifies his authoritarian crackdown with violent ICE raids and
National Guard deployments.

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-email-20251022.oXoxVM&refcode=em20251022-5552&t=1002&akid=5552%2E420207%2E3-KYDH ]A photo of Pramila speaking to the crowd, next to another photo of
Pramila smiling in front of a large crowd.
Pramila spoke to the No Kings protesters in Seattle

Our Resistance is growing! Now, we need to make it our everyday work.
That’s why I started Resistance Labs—to help our growing movement
understand how to best fight authoritarians and take action right in your
community.

That’s why I was THRILLED that on Sunday, more than 1,000 people from 41
states and 4 countries took the energy of No Kings Day and turned out for
our 10th Resistance Lab training, this one focused on immigration justice.

Resistance Lab is all about taking your anger, frustration and energy and
turning it into effective, nonviolent action. We consulted with the top
experts from around the world on how democracies crumble and what people
can do about it.

In just five months, we have trained more than 17,000 people from all 50
states and over half a dozen countries.

Sunday’s session was amazing! We focused specifically on immigration, how
Trump is using our own military and supercharging ICE to terrorize our
communities and conduct mass deportations of people—just for how they
look, what language they speak or what street corner they hang out on. And
if they can do this to immigrants—including US citizens—they can do it to
anyone. Resistance Lab helps people understand what is going on, how to
nonviolently fight back, and how to build the momentum we need to resist
Trump’s unconstitutional and illegal actions.

Truly, this is the most inspiring and hopeful work I have been involved
in—building people’s power in this crucial moment. And,
Peter, we need to keep it up!

I fund all of this organizing through my campaign. I’m one of very few
members of Congress who actually uses the campaign to build the people’s
power through this kind of grassroots organizing. I do it because I
believe this is the real answer. To keep up this Resistance Labs work, I
really need your help. Every donation you make goes straight to Resistance
Labs.

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-email-20251022.oXoxVM&refcode=em20251022-5552&amount=3&t=1003&akid=5552%2E420207%2E3-KYDH ]So Peter,
can I count on you to make a donation of $3, or whatever
amount works for you, to help us keep resisting?

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-email-20251022.oXoxVM&amount=3&refcode=em20251022-5552&t=1022&akid=5552%2E420207%2E3-KYDH ]Contribute $3

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/50885?utm_source=em20251022-5552&t=1023&akid=5552%2E420207%2E3-KYDH ]And if you’d like to join us for the next Resistance Lab, you can
click here to sign up for our November session now.

This weekend proves what we can accomplish when we come together. If we
keep it up, we can defend our democracy and finally build a government
that works for all of us.

In solidarity,

Pramila Jayapal

name: Texas Organizing Project
subject: Don’t forget to vote! / ¡No olvides votar! 🗳️ 🎃 🍂
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/PNG%202023%20TOP%20Newsletter%20Header.png]
Lea el boletín en español abajo [#Español]
HEAD TO THE POLLS:
Cast your ballot on Texas statewide propositions
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Smaller%20-%20Vote%20person%20table%20ballot%20box.jpeg]
TEXANS! Early voting is underway for our state's constitutional amendments election. A number of local races and special elections are also taking place across the state, so don't miss your chance to have your voice heard at the polls.
Voters in our state will weigh in on 17 statewide propositions this election. If approved by the majority of voters, these ballot propositions become constitutional amendments, which are then enshrined in our state constitution.
https://www.facebook.com/share/p/1BMe2tcAyV/ [https://www.facebook.com/share/p/1BMe2tcAyV/]
Early voting goes through Oct. 31. Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 4.
Access more early voting information here. [https://www.votetexas.gov/voting/where.html]
TAKE ACTION:
Sign the petition against unfair rent price-setting in Dallas
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Rent%20increase%20form.jpg]
If you’re a Dallas resident, there's still time to sign our petition calling for fairer rent practices in the city!
TOP and DFW housing justice allies are urging the City of Dallas to ban the use of property management software RealPage [https://finance.yahoo.com/news/what-is-realpage--and-why-is-it-being-blamed-for-raising-everyones-rent-184647022.html] , as well as other real estate platforms that engage in algorithmic price setting.
RealPage is under investigation by the U.S. Dept. of Justice and is facing multiple lawsuits from states and cities for violating antitrust laws.
https://secure.everyaction.com/NXgD0nS8F02LVZwJDOVXgQ2 [https://secure.everyaction.com/NXgD0nS8F02LVZwJDOVXgQ2]
For more information on this campaign, contact Iman at ibouzid@organizetexas.org [ibouzid@organizetexas.org] .
NOVEMBER 1:
Honor Día De Los Muertos with TOP in Houston
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Smaller%20-%20Dia%20de%20los%20Muertos%20skull.jpg]
YOU'RE INVITED: Join Houston TOP staff and members on Saturday, Nov. 1, from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. as we celebrate Dia De Los Muertos with community allies at MECA.
Come enjoy the food, festivities, and fellowship. We hope to see you there!
For more event information and to RSVP, email Andres at arodriguez@organizetexas.org [arodriguez@organizetexas.org] .
TOP Tip: Declutter your digital life by doing Opt Out October
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Online%20privacy%20security.jpg]
There's never a bad time to boost your online security and privacy. A great way to start is by practicing good digital hygiene! Learn more about Opt Out October and how you can benefit. [https://www.eff.org/deeplinks/2025/09/opt-out-october-daily-tips-protect-your-privacy-and-security]
Español
VAYAN A LAS URNAS:
Emiten su voto sobre las propuestas estatales de nuestro estado
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Smaller%20-%20Vote%20person%20table%20ballot%20box.jpeg]
TEJANOS! La votación anticipada para las enmiendas constitucionales de nuestro estado ya está en marcha. También se están llevando a cabo varias elecciones locales y especiales en todo Texas, así que no pierdas la oportunidad de hacer que tu voz se escuche en las urnas.
Los votantes de nuestro estado decidirán sobre 17 proposiciones estatales en esta elección. Si la mayoría las aprueba, estas medidas se convertirán en enmiendas constitucionales que pasarán a formar parte de nuestra constitución estatal.
https://www.facebook.com/share/p/1BMe2tcAyV/ [https://www.facebook.com/share/p/1BMe2tcAyV/]
La votación anticipada se extiende hasta el 31 de octubre. El día de las elecciones es el martes 4 de noviembre.
Accedan a más información sobre la votación anticipada aquí. [https://www.votetexas.gov/voting/where.html]
ACTÚA:
Firma la petición contra la fijación injusta de precios de alquiler en Dallas
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Rent%20increase%20form.jpg]
Si vives en Dallas, todavía estás a tiempo de firmar nuestra petición para exigir prácticas de renta más justas en la ciudad!
TOP y nuestros aliados por la justicia de vivienda en el área de DFW estamos pidiendo a la Ciudad de Dallas que prohíba el uso del software de administración de propiedades RealPage [https://finance.yahoo.com/news/what-is-realpage--and-why-is-it-being-blamed-for-raising-everyones-rent-184647022.html] , así como de otras plataformas inmobiliarias que utilizan algoritmos para manipular los precios de la renta.
RealPage está siendo investigado por el Departamento de Justicia de Los Estados Unidos y enfrenta múltiples demandas de estados y ciudades por violar las leyes de antimonopolio.
https://secure.everyaction.com/NXgD0nS8F02LVZwJDOVXgQ2 [https://secure.everyaction.com/NXgD0nS8F02LVZwJDOVXgQ2]
Para más información sobre esta campaña, contacta con Iman en ibouzid@organizetexas.org [ibouzid@organizetexas.org] .
1 DE NOVIEMBRE:
Honre el Día De Los Muertos con TOP en Houston
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Smaller%20-%20Dia%20de%20los%20Muertos%20skull.jpg]
ESTÁS INVITADO: Únete al personal y miembros de Houston TOP el sábado 1 de noviembre, de 11 a.m. a 7 p.m., para celebrar el Día de los Muertos con aliados de la comunidad en MECA.
Ven a disfrutar de la comida, las festividades y la camaradería. ¡Esperamos verte allí!
Para más información sobre el evento y confirmar tu asistencia, escribe a Andrés a arodriguez@organizetexas.org [arodriguez@organizetexas.org] .
Consejos de TOP: Ordena tu vida digital con la campaña Opt Out October
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Online%20privacy%20security.jpg]
Nunca es mal momento para reforzar tu seguridad y privacidad en línea. ¡Una excelente manera de empezar es practicar una buena higiene digital! Descubre más sobre la opción de exclusión voluntaria de octubre y cómo puedes beneficiarte. [https://www.eff.org/deeplinks/2025/09/opt-out-october-daily-tips-protect-your-privacy-and-security]

name: Angela Gonzales-Torres
subject: Dozens of Dem candidates won’t commit to backing Jeffries, and I’m one of them
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JUSTICE DEMOCRATS
body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter, I’m fed up with politicians
that stand for nothing while our democracy crumbles. And I know I’m not
alone — many Angelenos feel this way.

The Trump administration is waging a relentless war on our communities.
ICE raids are terrorizing families, shuttering small businesses, and
leaving our neighbors too afraid to step outside.

And what are Democratic leaders like Hakeem Jeffries doing? Tweets, press
conferences, and strongly-worded statements.

While working people suffer, party elites are throwing their hands up.
They would rather protect their own power instead of fighting for ours.

We deserve better.

That’s why I’m running for Congress: because I believe in a Democratic
Party led by the people, not by billionaires, corporations, or career
politicians.

When I’m in Congress, I cannot support Hakeem Jeffries as the leader of
this Party, because I believe in leadership that answers to communities,
not corporations.

And I’m not alone: the vast majority of candidates for Congress running in
Dem primaries nationwide feel this way. And that’s why I told Axios this
week, we should welcome new leadership in the Democratic Party.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20251022-agt.SZa0Bx&refcode=em20251022-37128&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=37128%2E1203867%2E7ACskx ]Scoop: Dozens of Dem candidates won’t commit to backing Jeffries

The truth is, our party is at a crossroads and everyone knows it.

The Democratic party can continue to let billionaires and out-of-touch
politicians call the shots, ignoring the pain of working people, or it can
choose a new generation of leaders ready to take on greed, corruption, and
oligarchy.

I’m choosing the people. Always.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20251022-agt.SZa0Bx&refcode=em20251022-37128&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1003&akid=37128%2E1203867%2E7ACskx ]If you’re ready to help shake up the status quo, start here. Can you
join our movement and chip in anything you can today to support our work?

In solidarity,

Angela Gonzales-Torres

body:
Traveling across the state, meeting with voters, and bringing our lower costs message to communities everywhere takes serious resources.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=40300%2E3422442%2EkWj97m)
Peter,
Katie Porter was on the road last week, meeting with Californians across the state.
She spent Saturday at a **No Kings protest** , standing shoulder to shoulder with Californians who are fed up with Donald Trump’s corruption, lawlessness, and attacks on our democracy. Katie knows California needs a tough fighter to stand up for our rights and liberties—that’s exactly why she’s running for Governor.
[](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20251022_1_ak.7G8pZP&refcode=em20251022-40300&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=40300%2E3422442%2EkWj97m)
She also joined the **UC Student & Policy Center** in Sacramento to share her vision for the next generation of Californians—a place where students can get a good-paying job and afford to stay after they graduate. As a single mom of three, Katie knows California’s next governor has to make California affordable for young people and working families alike.
[](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20251022_1_ak.7G8pZP&refcode=em20251022-40300&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=40300%2E3422442%2EkWj97m)

name: Sarah McBride
subject: Trump’s raiding health care to reward billionaire donors
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
Republicans want to raid health care to fund tax breaks for billionaires and power their authoritarian agenda — we can’t let them get away with it.
#
I recently joined _The Bulwark_ to make something very clear about this government shutdown — and I need to make sure you hear it too.
**This crisis didn’t just happen by accident. Republicans planned it.** We all know they’ll stop at nothing to gut affordable health care, but at the heart of this shutdown, what they’re really after is something even darker: Control.
**Because the GOP’s push to raid our health care is inextricably tied to their authoritarian power grab.**
[****](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20251022-1.CxkB1C&refcode=em20251022-2427&%3Bamount=5&t=1&akid=2427%2E21716%2E66PuYX)
Trump made an unholy alliance in the last election with tech oligarchs and billionaires. He told them, “ _You fund my campaign, and I’ll pay you off with massive tax breaks.”_ And he’s doing just that — and paying for it by raiding people’s health care.
When we cut off his capacity to raid folks’ health care to fund tax cuts for billionaires, we’re also addressing his authoritarian consolidation of power.
That is why this fight is so important — our health care, our democracy, and the future of our country are all at stake. And it’s why I refuse to back down.
[**So if you’re able to today, please pitch in to help fuel this movement — because protecting health care and defeating authoritarianism is always worth fighting for.**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20251022-1.CxkB1C&refcode=em20251022-2427&amount=5&t=2&akid=2427%2E21716%2E66PuYX)

subject: ICE is a criminal, rogue agency that regularly breaks the law.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
New York City does not mess around.
#
ICE is a criminal, rogue agency that regularly breaks the law, illegally assaults U.S. citizens and noncitizens alike, and is held to virtually NO respectable standards whatsoever.
New Yorkers protect each other. We are not going to allow masked cowards to intimidate, abuse, and disappear people because they put a napkin over their face.
When you see them, **blow the whistle**.
They have been disappearing children and innocent people — _including_ U.S. citizens, before anyone thinks it's an excuse to violate human rights depending on one's status — which for the record, is WRONG.
Do _not_ make their life easy. Make it as hard as possible to break the law and disrupt our way of life.
In solidarity,
Alexandria

Friend, In a moment, I’m going to ask you to chip in **[$3](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/117801381/577684522/-530796408?refcode=em-10.22.25-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNmM4NzA2MDktOWZhZi1mMDExLThlNjEtNjA0NWJkZWQ4YmE0IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=868alo6zJAsyKIpfgjDsJftGl4WiBnhAtB4CFziLTvo=)** , but first let me explain why your support is so important. The Central Valley is often overlooked – but it’s the beating heart of democracy. This is where César Chávez and the UFW organized and won dignity for working people. Subject: [New Report] A Supreme Court case that could rig control of the U.S. House
In one week, the Supreme Court will re-hear a case where they could strike down Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act and remove protections against discriminatory redistricting maps, which could lock in one-party rule of the U.S. House of Representatives.
According to a new joint report penned by my organization, Black Voters Matter, and Fair Fight Action, taking away this section of the Voting Rights Act would open the floodgates to discriminatory mapmaking, particularly in the South, effectively gutting the political power of Black voters and other voters of color.
**Our analysis shows that this could lock in an estimated 27 additional safe U.S. House seats for the GOP, with at least 19 in the South directly tied to striking down Section 2.** Combined with Republicans’ mid-decade gerrymandering scheme in states like Texas and Missouri, a ruling against Section 2 could allow them to cement one-party control of the U.S. House for at least a generation.
**It’s all part of the MAGA operation’s strategy to create a new “Solid South.”**
Black Voters Matter and Fair Fight Action are meeting this massive voter suppression attempt by organizing the strongest pro-voting backlash of Black voters and allies’ power we’ve ever seen. We’re supporting local leaders in key states, growing our grassroots networks, and demanding that the Supreme Court and Congress protect our maps from discriminatory redistricting ahead of the 2026 midterm elections and beyond.

The Voting Rights Act has been one of the most successful pieces of legislation in our country’s history. End of sentence. When it was passed, it had an immediate impact on increasing Black voter registration rates and protected Black voters’ access to the ballot.
And by prohibiting lawmakers of any party from adopting redistricting maps that have racially discriminatory effects, Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act works to fulfill the guarantee of the 14th and 15th Amendments that minority voters must have equal voting rights. A decision against Section 2 would be a huge loss for both Black Voters Matter and Fair Fight Action in our work to protect our freedom to vote.

| **Dear Friend,** I am writing to you today deeply concerned about the recent events that have shaken our community and our nation. **Last Friday night, two churches right here in North Carolina went up in flames. This is not just an act of vandalism; it is part of a growing assault on Christianity and our shared values in America. **As a pastor and a public servant, I am committed to ensuring that our faith and our freedoms are protected. But I cannot do this alone.
---
| [ ](https://markharrisforcongress.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=82117f51bb8b79bb18d514427&id=76b67c0538&e=4024c5123e)

| This is a moment that calls for clarity, courage, and action. Your support is crucial as we navigate these challenging times. Your contribution matters now more than ever.

**This is not just about politics; it’s about preserving the America we love—a nation where faith, family, and freedom are cherished and protected.** Your support will help ensure that we can continue to stand up for these principles, even in the face of adversity.
